title: The gate that was too expensive
kicker: World 7 · Decide Where It Matters · Level 2

job.text:
Someone built the billing pipeline with a hard gate on every step. It's slow and brittle, and the hard gates on the wording still can't make it any better. Relax the gates that don't need to be hard — without un-gating a step that has one right answer.

Every step starts hard-gated. Turn a chip on to relax that step to heuristic. Leave a chip off to keep that step's hard gate.

naivePrompt: Gate it all to be safe.
basePrompt: Gate it all to be safe.

text.plain: Relax the payment-plan suggestion to heuristic — it has no single right answer, so a hard gate buys nothing.
text.tech: Set step 3 (payment plan) gate: heuristic — no exact answer to gate against.

text.plain: Relax the apology wording to heuristic — wording has no one right answer.
text.tech: Set step 5 (apology wording) gate: heuristic — open-ended text.

text.plain: Relax the greeting to heuristic — a greeting has no single right answer.
Relax the invoice total to save time — but it has exactly one right answer, so its gate must stay hard.
text.tech: Set step 1 (invoice total) gate: heuristic — but a wrong total ships if you do.

text.plain: Relax the account balance to save time — but a lookup has one right value, so its gate must stay hard.
text.tech: Set step 4 (account balance) gate: heuristic — but a wrong balance ships if you do.

rules.claim: A right-answer gate was relaxed — and a wrong total or balance shipped.
rules.feedback: You traded away a gate you needed. The invoice total and the balance each have one right answer — their gates stay hard no matter how slow. You can't buy speed by un-gating an exact step.

output.source: a right-answer gate traded away for speed

rules.claim: Open steps relaxed; the invoice total and balance stay hard-gated. Faster, still exact where it counts.
rules.feedback: Right trade. You relaxed the judgment steps and kept the exact ones gated. Faster, and still correct where correctness has one answer.
rules.lesson: Spend your gates where there's a right answer.

output.source: gates kept where there is a right answer

rules.claim: The wording and recommendation are still hard-gated — the pipeline stays slow and brittle.
rules.feedback: Still too expensive. Hard-gating the wording and the recommendation catches nothing and costs a lot. Relax the open steps.
rules.lesson: Gating the open steps is pure cost.

hints.nudge: Which of these steps has one right answer? Those keep the hard gate.
hints.gap: The total and the balance must stay gated — relax the other steps.
hints.moves: Relax the payment-plan recommendation and the apology wording; keep the invoice total and the balance gated. (You can relax the greeting too — it's open as well.)

whatYouDoDifferently.rewrite: Relax the open steps, keep the exact ones gated → fast and still correct where it counts.

template.plain: This is over-engineered — it treats every step as critical. Keep hard checks only on the steps with one right answer; let the judgment steps run loose. Tell me which you relaxed and why.
template.tech: This pipeline gates every step. Keep gate: hard only on steps with a single correct value; set the rest to gate: heuristic. Report which gates you relaxed and the cost-of-wrong rationale for each.

notes: ChatGPT: have it identify which gates actually earn their cost.
Copilot in Excel: keep formulas on the exact steps; drop needless validation on the text.
A chat AI that can't run code: you decide which steps are truly must-be-exact — and never relax the ones with one right answer to save time.
